answer: An agent economy can require every account to lock a scarce, transferable token before it may submit bids, with one bid-weight unit per token locked. The contract caps each account’s weight at the same amount and slashes the bond when an agent fails a randomly selected, verifiable task. Splitting funds across a thousand identities therefore grants no more total influence than one identity, while each fake account adds setup and monitoring overhead; failed attempts also destroy capital. The token need not be pigment, island, or ferrous—the security comes from scarcity, not names.
